To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

four subjects who were treated with the antipsychotic medication quetiapine experienced a significant reduction in weight gain when they were concurrently treated with conjugated linolecic acid and green-tea extract.

four patients with social anxiety disorder who had been treated with the antipsychotic agent quetiapine experienced weight loss and decreased body fat percentage following self-administration of dietary supplements containing conjugated linoleiic acid and green extract tea.

(1) weight gain is a serious side-effect of many antipsychotic medications, which may be exacerbated by sedentary lifestyles and a diet rich in saturated fats and simple sugars, (2) weight gain may further compound the psychological distress of psychiatric illness, (3) weight loss is a desirable goal for psychiatric patients and (4) weight loss is possible with the use of dietary supplements.

the potential role of dietary supplements in the treatment of mental illness, particularly weight gain associated with psychiatric treatment.
the role of green tea and conjugate linoleic acid in reducing weight gain associated with psychiatric medications.
the potential of conjugated linolaic acid and green-tea extract in the management of weight-gain in patients treated with atypical antipsyhcotic medications.

green tea and CLA may be effective adjunctive treatments to help reduce weight gain in patients treated with antipsychotic medications.

the use of dietary supplements in patients with psychiatric disorders is common, and should be considered in clinical practice.
